name: stuck-page
description:
A Cortex XDR that ignores the search_from/search_to window and answers every request with the same full page of a hundred. The walk's own exit is a page shorter than the window, which this shape never produces, so before the repeated-page check it spun until the task timed out with nothing in the log to say why.

This is the scenario the page ceiling used to be responsible for, and it is why the ceiling is no longer the primary guard: at the derived ceiling of 100,000 pages a stuck tenant would have been hammered a hundred thousand times before anything stopped it. The repeated-page check settles it in two requests instead, and can never truncate genuine data because it only fires on a page that adds nothing.

request_count is exact at 2: the first window, and the one re-fetch that reveals the repeat. A walk that does not notice issues more; one that stops too early issues fewer.

The route matching search_from 200 exists ONLY as a terminator. Serving the stuck page with when_exhausted=repeat_last alone would make a regressed walk run forever and fail this scenario by TIMING OUT rather than by failing an assertion; with the terminator it stops one request later and fails on request_count, requests_absent and the missing log line instead.

total_count is deliberately far larger than what is served: the walk must terminate on the data alone, never on a count the API is free to omit or to get wrong. It is what the truncation line reports as the 'available' half, so log_contains pins the retrieved-versus-available shape as well as the reason.

The check runs BEFORE the page is reported, so the repeated records never reach runZero -- which is what keeps asset_count at 1 and the ids unique. Every page carries a full hundred records because a shorter page is exactly what ends the walk; the first record is a real endpoint so the scenario still proves rows are parsed and reported, and the other ninety-nine have neither agent_id nor endpoint_id and are skipped.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in happy: the id is the bare Cortex agent id with no tenant scope.

log_contains: cortex-xdr: paging stopped after 2 pages: the API returned the same page twice. Retrieved 1/340000 available assets
